paragraphs.title: Reopening the Temple and the Need for Its Repair

easy.explanation: The passage begins by describing Hezekiah's reign.
easy.q: Who was the king described at the beginning of the passage?

answers: He opened and repaired its doors
He moved it to another place
easy.explanation: Hezekiah opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
easy.q: What did Hezekiah do to the house of the LORD in the first year of his reign?

easy.explanation: He brought in the priests and Levites and gathered them in the east street.
easy.q: Whom did Hezekiah gather in the east street?

answers: To prepare the house of the LORD for renewed service
medium.explanation: He wanted the Temple cleansed and prepared for worship again.
medium.q: Why did Hezekiah tell the Levites to sanctify themselves and the house of the LORD?

answers: Their sins brought punishment and trouble
medium.explanation: He said that the LORD's wrath had brought trouble upon Judah and Jerusalem because of their unfaithfulness.
medium.q: What connection did Hezekiah make between the sins of the fathers and the condition of Judah and Jerusalem?

answers: They turned away from the LORD
medium.explanation: The expression describes turning away from the LORD and His habitation.
medium.q: What does the expression “turned their backs” mean in this passage?

answers: He repaired the worship of God before other matters
He built an army before repairing the Temple
He postponed the Temple's repair until the end of his reign
challenge.explanation: He opened and began restoring the house of the LORD in the first month of the first year of his reign.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the order of Hezekiah's actions about his priorities?

answers: To explain the need for repentance and renewed devotion to the LORD
To praise the actions of the fathers
To abolish the work of the priests
challenge.explanation: He connected forsaking the LORD with judgment and therefore called the people back to covenant faithfulness.
challenge.q: Why did Hezekiah mention the sins of earlier generations before calling for a renewed covenant?

answers: He acted immediately at the beginning of his reign
He waited until the end of his reign
He sent the people somewhere else
challenge.explanation: The Temple doors were opened in the first year and first month of his reign.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the urgency Hezekiah saw in repairing the Temple?

easy.explanation: The Levites arose, gathered their brethren, and sanctified themselves for the work.
easy.q: Who arose to carry out the work of cleansing the Temple?

easy.explanation: The priests brought out all the uncleanness found in the Temple.
easy.q: What did the priests bring out of the house of the LORD?

easy.explanation: The Levites carried it out to the brook Kidron.
easy.q: Where did the Levites carry the uncleanness?

answers: They sanctified themselves and came to cleanse the house of the LORD
They closed the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: They sanctified themselves and came according to the king's commandment and the word of the LORD.
medium.q: What did the Levites do after gathering their brethren?

answers: They were prepared and sanctified again
They were carried to the brook Kidron
medium.explanation: The vessels were prepared and sanctified and placed before the altar of the LORD.
medium.q: What happened to the vessels that King Ahaz had cast away?

medium.explanation: Ahaz had cast the Temple vessels away instead of using them properly.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “cast away” mean?

answers: Each group had a particular role in the cleansing
Only the Levites were allowed to enter the house of the LORD
The priests did not participate in the cleansing
challenge.explanation: The priests removed the uncleanness from the inner part, and the Levites carried it outside.
challenge.q: What does the division of duties between the priests and Levites show?

answers: The worship service required sanctified vessels
The vessels were intended as homes for the Levites
The vessels were used to build the court
challenge.explanation: The neglected vessels had to be prepared and sanctified before they could serve in worship.
challenge.q: Why was preparing the Temple vessels again part of restoring the service?

answers: Sanctifying themselves, removing the uncleanness, and carrying it to Kidron
Offering sacrifices, building a wall, and gathering the people
Singing, lighting lamps, and closing the Temple
challenge.explanation: The workers first sanctified themselves, then removed the uncleanness and carried it away.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence of the cleansing described in the passage?

paragraphs.title: Renewing Sacrifices and Music in the Temple

easy.explanation: Hezekiah gathered the rulers of the city and went up to the house of the LORD.
easy.q: Who went up to the house of the LORD with Hezekiah?

easy.explanation: Seven bullocks, seven rams, and seven lambs were brought.
easy.q: How many bullocks, rams, and lambs were brought for the offering?

easy.explanation: The Levites used cymbals, psalteries, and harps.
easy.q: Which instruments did the Levites use?

answers: For atonement for the kingdom, the Temple, and Judah
To feed all the people of the city
medium.explanation: The offerings were made as a sin offering for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and Judah.
medium.q: For what purpose were the offerings brought by Hezekiah and the city rulers?

answers: The song of the LORD and the trumpets began
medium.explanation: The song began with the trumpets and the instruments ordained by David.
medium.q: What happened when the burnt offering began?

medium.explanation: The trumpeters sounded their trumpets while the singers sang.
medium.q: What does “sounded” mean in the phrase about the trumpeters?

answers: They worshipped, sang, and joined in praise
They carried uncleanness to the brook
challenge.explanation: The congregation worshipped, while the singers sang and the trumpeters sounded.
challenge.q: How did the congregation participate besides bringing offerings?

answers: It included both sacrificial worship and praise
It was only a military ceremony
It was only a preparation of the vessels
challenge.explanation: The service joined offerings with music, singing, worship, and praise.
challenge.q: What does the combination of sacrifices, singing, and trumpets show about the renewed service?

answers: To show that the musical order followed an established and authorized pattern
To explain how the Temple was built
To identify who offered the sacrifices
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the music with the commandment given through David, Gad, and Nathan.
challenge.q: Why is the commandment of David, Gad, and Nathan mentioned?

paragraphs.title: Thank Offerings and the People's Generosity

answers: The Temple doors to the palace
easy.explanation: Hezekiah told the people to bring sacrifices and thank offerings into the house of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Hezekiah ask the people to bring after the sacrificial service?

answers: Those who were of a free heart
easy.explanation: Those with willing or generous hearts brought burnt offerings.
easy.q: Who brought burnt offerings in addition to the offerings brought by the congregation?

easy.explanation: The congregation brought threescore and ten, or seventy, bullocks.
easy.q: How many bullocks did the congregation bring for a burnt offering?

answers: Sacrifices, thank offerings, and burnt offerings
medium.explanation: Hezekiah called for sacrifices and thank offerings, and generous people brought burnt offerings.
medium.q: What kinds of offerings did the people bring according to the passage?

medium.explanation: The passage says that three thousand sheep were consecrated.
medium.q: Which number describes the sheep brought as consecrated things?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes people who gave willingly and generously.
medium.q: What does “of a free heart” mean in this context?

answers: The restoration became a shared effort of the king and the people
Only the king was responsible for worship
The people opposed the Temple service
challenge.explanation: After the king's offerings, the congregation and generous individuals brought offerings as well.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from the king's offerings to the people's offerings?

answers: The large numbers of cattle and sheep brought
Only one person brought an offering
challenge.explanation: The passage lists seventy bullocks, one hundred rams, two hundred lambs, six hundred oxen, and three thousand sheep.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the extent of the people's participation?

answers: They expressed participation and gratitude after the service was restored
They replaced the cleansing of the Temple
They were used to build the Temple doors
challenge.explanation: After the Temple service was renewed, the people were invited to participate through offerings and thanksgiving.
challenge.q: What connection is there between the sacrifices and thank offerings and the purpose of restoring the Temple?

paragraphs.title: Completion of the Service and the People's Joy

easy.explanation: The Levites helped the priests until the work was ended.
easy.q: Who helped the priests flay the burnt offerings?

easy.explanation: The priests were too few to flay all the burnt offerings.
easy.q: How is the number of priests described?

answers: Because God had prepared the people
Because a palace had been built
easy.explanation: They rejoiced because God had prepared the people for the restored service.
easy.q: Why did Hezekiah and all the people rejoice?

answers: There were too few priests and many offerings
The Levites did not know their duties
medium.explanation: The priests could not flay all the burnt offerings because they were too few.
medium.q: Why did the priests need the help of the Levites?

answers: Burnt offerings, the fat of peace offerings, and drink offerings
medium.explanation: The passage mentions abundant burnt offerings, the fat of peace offerings, and drink offerings.
medium.q: What did the renewed service of the house of the LORD include?

medium.explanation: The verse says the thing was done suddenly, meaning it happened quickly and unexpectedly.
medium.q: What does “suddenly” mean in the final verse?

answers: They could cooperate to complete the Temple service
Only the Levites were permitted to serve
The priests and Levites worked entirely separately
challenge.explanation: The Levites helped the priests until the work was completed.
challenge.q: What does the Levites' help show about the relationship between the priests and Levites?

answers: Their willing and rapid participation was seen as something God enabled
The people did not participate at all
The Temple was immediately closed again
challenge.explanation: The people joined the service quickly, and the passage attributes this preparation to God.
challenge.q: Why is the people's joy described as a result of God preparing their hearts?

answers: The reopening of the Temple leads to ordered service and the people's joy
The Temple was opened and then immediately closed
The people left before the service began
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with Hezekiah opening the house of the LORD and ends with the service restored and the people rejoicing.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the beginning and the end of the passage?
